solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hoarder, member that is collecting silver

indicators.note: the member is said to gather up the silver, so its letters go round the metal's symbol

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
AG is the chemical symbol for silver
i.e. (id est) is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Some acquisitive club member or politician is gathering up silverware.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird of that name is famed in folklore for stealing and stashing shiny objects, so it stands for any collector of trinkets.

clue.text: Male and kind maiden help farm girl

parts.note: ilk means kind or sort
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
aid means help

explanation.surface: A man and a kindly young woman lend a hand to a girl working on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, recorded as M.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairy worker who draws milk from cows is traditionally a young woman on the farm.

clue.text: Restaurant welcoming leader of order, a primate

indicators.note: the restaurant takes in a guest, so its letters surround the other piece

parts.note: a grill is a restaurant serving grilled food

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of 'order'

explanation.surface: A restaurant receives the head of a religious order, who happens to be an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: The great ape is one of the largest members of the primate order of mammals.

clue.text: Part of Irish parliament I upset — epic tale!

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word on its head, so the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament, the Oireachtas

explanation.surface: Someone recounts how they overturned a chamber of the Irish parliament, a heroic saga.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's poem about the siege of Troy is the archetypal Greek epic.

clue.text: Saw new father keeping quiet where an exchange may take place!

definitions.text: where an exchange may take place!

indicators.note: new means the letters of saw are made into a fresh arrangement
father holds on to the quiet sign, so it sits inside him

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
sh is the instruction to be quiet

explanation.surface: A child saw that a new father kept things hushed, as at a place of trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A swap shop is a place or event where people trade goods with one another instead of paying money.

clue.text: Motto when a sword is used

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are put to use in a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier's motto for when the blade is drawn.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase is the motto of the British Special Air Service regiment, whose badge features a winged dagger.

clue.text: Director in cheap pink pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are a mess and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A film director spotted wearing inexpensive pink trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers but works as British slang for rubbish, signalling that the letters are jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Sam Peckinpah was the American film-maker behind The Wild Bunch and Straw Dogs.

clue.text: Talk incessantly about old weapon

indicators.note: the phrase for talking incessantly wraps around the abbreviation for old

parts.note: to harp on is to talk about something repeatedly and tediously

explanation.surface: Someone drones on and on about an antique weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbed spear thrown or fired to catch whales and large fish is a hunting weapon.

clue.text: Pair to remove and replace French writer

parts.note: to oust someone is to drive them out and take their place

explanation.surface: A couple are to be thrown out and substituted by a French author.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Proust was the French novelist who wrote In Search of Lost Time.

clue.text: Poet fooling about no end

indicators.note: the word for fooling about loses its final letter

parts.note: larking is fooling about or playing pranks

explanation.surface: A poet who never stops messing around.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Larkin was the English poet of The Whitsun Weddings and This Be The Verse.

clue.text: Business limited to composer's work

indicators.note: the word for business is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a concern is a business or firm

explanation.surface: A company whose activity is restricted to producing a composer's output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' is the business suffix Ltd in the surface, but here it trims the end off CONCERN.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a musical composition for a solo instrument and orchestra.

clue.text: Confront unpleasantness, as conductors usually do?

definitions.meaning: to accept the consequences of one's actions and meet trouble head on
taken literally, an orchestra's conductor stands looking towards the score and the players

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to accept criticism or punishment; read literally, it describes where a conductor looks during a performance.

clue.text: Play short tune, hit by American

indicators.note: the word for tune is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: a melody is a tune
to ram is to hit forcefully

explanation.surface: A brief tune gets struck by an American.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a sensational stage play with exaggerated characters and emotions.

clue.text: Superstars in papers almost lose out

parts.note: ID means identity papers

indicators.note: out means the remaining letters are shaken into a different order
the word lose is taken without its last letter

explanation.surface: Celebrities in the newspapers nearly miss out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims LOSE to LOS, and 'out' rearranges that to OLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Idols are figures worshipped by fans, such as pop or film celebrities.

clue.text: Very much out of one's comfort zone, like the non-swimmer here?

definitions.text: Very much out of one's comfort zone
definitions.meaning: facing a difficult situation with no experience of it
literally, someone who cannot swim placed in the part of a pool where the water is over their head

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being thrown into a challenge with no preparation; literally it is the part of a pool too deep to stand in.

clue.text: Drill team exercised — on this?

indicators.note: the drill team's letters are put through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: A squad doing drill works out on a piece of gym equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is an exercise machine with a moving belt on which one walks or runs in place.

clue.text: Said again in desert at resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, the letters are sorted again into another order

explanation.surface: Something repeated in a desert holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' seems to be a holiday spot but is read as re-sort, an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To restate is to say or express something once more.

clue.text: Knighted actor from Northern Ireland may in backing English stage

indicators.note: the tree sits inside the reversed pair of English and stage
backing means the pair of English and stage is read from the end

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
may is another name for the hawthorn tree or its blossom

explanation.surface: A knighted actor from Northern Ireland might back an English theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns E + LEG into GELE, and HAWTHORN goes 'in' it. 'may' looks like a verb but is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Nigel Hawthorne, star of Yes Minister and The Madness of King George, was knighted in 1999.

clue.text: Learned head removed — say again

indicators.note: the word for learned loses its first letter

parts.note: literate means educated or learned

explanation.surface: An educated person is beheaded, so repeat it.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to repeat or perform again.

clue.text: Iris, artist, in front of ship

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician
the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: Iris, a painter, stands at the prow of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iris' looks like the painter's first name but is the Greek goddess. 'in front of' splits into IN and 'front of ship'.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris was the Greek goddess personifying the arc of colours in the sky.

clue.text: Old calculator that may make a graduate swear endlessly

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts

indicators.note: the word for swear loses its last letter

parts.note: to cuss is to swear

explanation.surface: An outdated calculating device that might make a student curse incessantly.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads on wires has been used for counting and arithmetic since ancient times.

clue.text: Unpleasant ringing about money

indicators.note: the word for unpleasant forms a ring around the other piece

parts.note: bad means unpleasant
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A nasty phone call about cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is a slang term for money, as is dough.

clue.text: Garment to wear in car on bypass?

parts.note: the Mini is a classic small British car
to skirt is to go round or avoid

explanation.surface: Clothing to put on while driving along a ring road.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mini is also the car that gave this short garment its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniskirt is a very short skirt, an item of women's clothing.

clue.text: Small hotel behind part of golf club

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
aft means at the back, as on a ship

explanation.surface: A little hotel sits at the back of the golf club's grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golf club' suggests the clubhouse but means the stick a golfer swings.
explanation.definitionFit: The shaft is the long handle connecting a club's grip to its head.

clue.text: Girl in cold Greek city

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
Larissa is a city in Thessaly, central Greece

explanation.surface: A young woman feeling chilly in a Greek city.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarissa is a female given name, also the heroine of Richardson's novel.

clue.text: Good scope offered by initial moves

definitions.note: plural here, while the answer is a single opening, which may involve several moves

parts.note: ambit means scope or extent

explanation.surface: Plenty of room for manoeuvre is given by the opening moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess opening in which a piece is sacrificed for advantage is a gambit; more widely, any opening ploy.

clue.text: Detective novel starts in rural location of contract killing

parts.note: She is the adventure novel by H. Rider Haggard

indicators.note: the starts are the first letters of each of the following five words

explanation.surface: A crime novel begins in a countryside spot where a hired murder happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherlock Holmes is Conan Doyle's famous fictional detective.

clue.text: Boiled or oiled?

definitions.meaning: cooked slowly in liquid, as meat in a casserole

explanation.definitionFit: Stewing is slow simmering; as slang the same word means drunk, matching oiled.
